items.evidence: After the title the overview opens '## The bottom line' with '**1. What FRUS answers directly.**', then '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**', then '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**', followed by a Scope paragraph and 'Decisions this needs from you'; the first '## Findings' heading comes only after all three parts.

Every figure names its set and base: 'about 2,900 of the 57,000 documents in the Latin American parts of the series, roughly one in twenty'; 'about three in five of those, judging from a sample of forty'; '30 of the 45 documents I rely on, and about two in three of the 2,900 candidates'; 'only about one candidate in fourteen carries such a footnote'; 'more than half (263 of 476) in 1950–79'; 'it did in 552 of 553'; 'I read forty of its hits: 23 ... 2 ... 15'; '123 documents against 65'. No percent sign or bare percentage occurs. The nearest to a bare figure is 'about 14 documents in 100 against 16', where the second number's base ('documents in 100', elsewhere in the series) is carried by the parallel phrase; it is still a rate of a named set, so it passes.

All 45 distinct documents the overview cites appear at least once as the printed edition with a history.state.gov link, e.g. 'Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1900, Document 530, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1900/d530' and 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volumes X/XI/XII, Microfiche Supplement, American Republics; Cuba 1961–1962; Cuban Missile Crisis and Aftermath, Document 109, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v10-12mSupp/d109' (53 links, 45 distinct documents, matching the collection's 45 document entries). No document is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone. One back-reference is abbreviated and unlinked, in Finding 2: '(FRUS 1948, The Western Hemisphere, Volume IX, Document 7)', for a document already cited in full with its link in the bottom line and twice in Finding 1. The collection's introduction text uses the short form 'FRUS 1877, Document 222' without links, but its document entries carry the identifiers by format.

Part 3 states each gap as a search: '(a) ... I searched the Latin American parts of all 553 volumes for recognition within six words of a government, regime, junta or administration. That finds about 1,150 documents dated 1861–1919, of which only six are internal memoranda ... the same test on document headings finds tens of thousands of memoranda across the series and nothing for a phrase that cannot occur'; '(b) "Wilson Doctrine" and "Mann Doctrine" appear in no document of the series, "Tobar Doctrine" in one, "Betancourt Doctrine" in three and "Estrada Doctrine" in 25 of the Latin American documents (the phrase reads literally the same way in 24 of the 25 ...)'; '(c) Spanish recognition vocabulary appears in only eleven of the 57,000 documents ... a search of that data for the ministries' names in English and Spanish found them only in its word-frequency tables and its registry of persons'; '(d) ... only about 400 documents dated in the 1980s, against about 3,200 for the 1970s'; closing with 'The controls for these searches were a phrase that must occur in nearly every volume (it did in 552 of 553) and an impossible phrase that must occur in none (it occurred in none).' Only (c)'s terms are described generically rather than listed.

A scan of the overview finds no SQL keyword, no table or column name (no volume_id, document_id, volume_structures, body_text or the like), no backtick, no file path (no /Users/, .json, .db, .log or .md), and no frus-style id pair outside a history.state.gov URL; the only id-like strings are the 53 history.state.gov links J3 requires. Counts are described in words ('the full-text index of all 553 volumes', 'the reference data shipped with the app', 'its word-frequency tables and its registry of persons'), and the memo is referred to without a path: 'The exact counts, the queries behind them and the files that hold them are in the memo.'

judge:r1.rankingReason: r7: the richest evidence (58 documents, 1865–1980, the Legal Adviser's 1939 rules, per-period counts of what was asked such as 'election ... 106 of 1,131') with footnote-vs-text discipline and a detailed two-channel archive; its only blemish is abbreviated '(Document 227, https://...)' back-references. r2: the strongest measurement of the scope and the limits (every zero carries its terms, volumes and the 'Department of State'/impossible-string controls), full citations throughout, a per-collection archival channel, and it catches the 1961 Cuban exile-government contamination. r6: 43 documents with the most precise archival pointers (lot, entry, NAID, dates, access) and a sharp Decisions section; its bullet quotes fall back to '(1877, Document 222)' without links. r1: 45 documents, the clearest reader-facing presentation (every block quote fully cited and linked), the best treatment of the 'what did it ask' half (Haiti 1915 treaty, Chile 1932 assurances, the Dominican seven points of 1963, Bolivia 1964 pledges) and a thoughtful cannot-get section on doctrine labels and Spanish vocabulary; one unlinked back-reference and some over-long sentences. r5: 56 documents reaching to Nicaragua 1979 with the cleanest citation form, but a thinner archival channel, lay glosses ('de facto means in fact') a historian does not need, and the 'political weapon' sentence attributed to Document 115 where other runs find it in Document 7. r9: 34 documents across the widest span and strong narrative findings, but its limits section counts the 'Tobar doctrine in eighty-eight documents' where r1 and r4 find the doctrine named once (the surname was counted) and says the Montevideo and Bogotá resolutions appear only in editors' footnotes, while other runs quote their text from printed documents. r4: careful scope-building and controls but only nineteen documents in the collection, the thinnest set a historian receives. r3: 38 documents from 25 volumes, admittedly 'a selection ... not a census', with most citations lacking the document number (sender-recipient-date or volume-plus-link only) and an off-topic Afghanistan document in the findings.

items.evidence: memo.md lines 9–14: "[N01] Coverage query, run first as the canary (INDEX): SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache; Result: `553|321749|1103|8481`"; queries.log line 3 holds the same command as the session's first call. I re-ran it against the read-only copy and got 553|321749|1103|8481.

memo.md line 3: "Every count below is conditional on this library, which holds **553 volumes**, the whole series [N01]. Nothing here is thin because of a partial library"; overview.md Scope: "I searched the Latin American material in all 553 volumes of the series as indexed on 25 October 2026". manifest.json lists 553 volumes and the volumes folder holds 553 XML files, so the count is right.

The memo cites every document as volume_id/document_id: "[Q01] frus1900/d530 (447 characters, finding 1)", the N05 sample table ("frus1892/d513 | Y | ..."), the section 17 table ("frus1900/d530 | Papers Relating to ... 1900, Document 530"); the overview gives volume title, document number and the history.state.gov address for each; collection entries carry volumeId/documentId ("volumeId": "frus1900", "documentId": "d530").

rowid occurs nowhere in memo.md, overview.md or collection.fruscollection. In queries.log it occurs 18 times, 17 as the sort tie-break of scripts/chapter_docs.py's chapter listings ("ORDER BY sd.date_iso, c.rowid") and once in a schema peek at line 22 ("FROM document_cache WHERE volume_id='frus1933v05' ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 6"); it is never selected, reported, joined on or used to name a document.

All 140 JOINs in queries.log use 17 distinct ON patterns, every document-level one on both columns, e.g. "ON sd.volume_id=f.volume_id AND sd.document_id=f.document_id" (92 times), "ON ds.volume_id=f.volume_id AND ds.document_id=f.document_id", "ON ec.volume_id=f.volume_id AND ec.document_id=f.document_id"; the only single-column joins ("ON h.volume_id=v.volume_id", "IN (SELECT volume_id FROM frus_documents ...)") are the per-volume control aggregation in N16. No script joins on document_id alone.

memo.md N02 (line 30): "apparatus = is_front_matter = 1 or is_editorial_note = 1 ... 321,749 rows = 9,580 front matter or editorial notes + ... + **305,438 numbered non-apparatus documents**. Every document count below is over that last set unless it says otherwise." Every logged count query carries "sd.apparatus=0"; overview Scope: "I left out front matter, the editors' notes, chapter headings and the duplicate second editions of two unrelated volumes".

Neither summary_text nor note_text appears in queries.log or in any script under scripts/ (grep over all of them); the 113 logged retrievals name their columns: "SELECT volume_id, document_id, header, dateline, source_note, body_text, length(body_text) FROM document_cache WHERE volume_id = ? AND document_id = ?" (N17), and the quotation checks select body_text only. The memo's "The summary_text and note_text columns were never selected" is borne out by the log.

cross_references is touched only as schema inspection: queries.log line 12 "SELECT group_concat(name || ':' || type, ', ') FROM pragma_table_info('cross_references')" and line 21's sqlite_master index listing. No query reads the table, and no cross-reference count appears in the memo, the overview or the collection, so the is_broken exclusion never arose.

memo.md N04: "the index drops punctuation and reduces words to a common form, so this is a proximity of word forms, not a phrase"; N14: "Spelling variants cannot be counted in the index (it merges forms), so the volumes' XML was scanned"; queries run on prefixes (recogn*, nonrecogn*, reconoc*) after inspecting the stemmed vocabulary (queries.log line 33: "SELECT term, doc, cnt FROM frus_documents_vocab WHERE term LIKE 'recogn%' ..."), and the literal-share test checks exact forms: "STRICT ... **37 of 40** ... TOLERANT ... **40 of 40**". Overview: "which treats different forms of a word as the same word".

citation_era is used only as a category label: N10's SQL "CASE WHEN ds.citation_era='decimal' THEN '(file number)' ELSE ds.series_name END AS series" with the result "decimal file numbers (Department of State, Record Group 59) **1,874**", and queries.log line 346 groups by it. The period "central decimal file for 1910–1963" in the overview comes from decimal-class-labels.json's glossable span (N12: "a key is glossed only when the document's own date is inside a glossable span, 1910-1963"), not from the column.

memo.md section 11 head: "CAME-FROM = the source note printed with the document (document_sources ...). POINTED-AT = what a footnote cites without printing (external_citations ...). The two are different questions and are not added." N10 (1,874 / 671 / 338 of 2,883) and N11 (208 of 2,883) are reported apart; the overview: "There are two channels, reported separately and never added together."

SQL is printed beside each count: N01, N16 (the UNION ALL control query), N02 (the scope breakdown SELECT), N03, N04 ("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frus_documents f JOIN s.scope_docs sd ... MATCH 'NEAR(recogn* government*, 6) OR ...'" → 2,883), N06 (452), N08 (template plus the 14 FTS expressions), N09, N10, N11, N13; scripts' SQL is rendered with parameters in queries.log ("# run by scripts/share_test.py ..."). Re-running N01, N04, N09, N10, N11, N13, the reconoc* count and the earliest-footnote query reproduced every figure (2883; 137/0 … 13/4; 1874/671; 208; 25|28, 1|1, 3|3, 0, 0; 11|24; 1910-12-06).

"2,883 of 57,144 is 5.0%, about one in twenty"; "STRICT ... **37 of 40**"; false-friend table cells "4251 of 28686 (14.8%) | 3604 of 28458 (12.7%) | 40300 of 248294 (16.2%)"; "1,874 of 2,883 is 65%, about two in three; 671 of 2,883 is 23%"; "**208** of 2,883 (7.2%, about one in fourteen)"; "73 of 2,832 is 2.6%"; every decade-table row prints hits and "dated docs in decade" beside the per-1,000 rate.

Clean.{0,3}Up'); N22: "series-facts-index.json (byNaId) has no row for any of these NAIDs" stated beside lookups of the same file that did return rows for 2198167 and 2838992.

memo.md line 3: "Nothing here is thin because of a partial library; where a result is thin it is thin in the corpus itself, and the memo says so." Thin results are flagged with their cause: N03/N03c "For 1981-88 the library holds one volume on South America ... and none on Central America or the Caribbean" (391 dated scope documents; 13 family C hits); N05 "a sample of forty gives a wide interval"; section 7 "the 1860s peak rests on one volume: frus1868p2 holds 51% of that decade's hits". memo.md N16 is one statement (queries.log line 59, 'positive: Department of State' UNION ALL 'negative: ZZZ_IMPOSSIBLE_ZZZ'): "positive 552 of 553 volumes with a hit (98,970 documents); the one volume with none is frus1919Parisv05 ... memo.md N14: "non-recognition hyphenated 123 documents (164 hits), closed 65 documents (72 hits), spaced 1 (1); de facto with a space 941 documents (hyphenated 2, closed 2); de jure 82; coup d'etat with the acute accent 197 documents, with a plain e 70; golpe 59; junta 1,212; recognise (British -s-) 16 documents; Spanish reconoc- 11 documents", with the full per-variant table (recognise_verb_s, unrecognised_s, defacto_closed ...); family W's FTS covers nonrecogn* / "non recogn*" / unrecogn*.

score:r1.notes: All four files are present (memo.md 691 lines, overview.md 168, queries.log 873, collection.fruscollection with 45 documents, 19 excerpts, 7 prose blocks and a generated archival-sources block), plus the run's bin/, raw/ (106 documents as .body.txt/.meta.txt), scripts/ and work/. The library is the complete series (553 index volumes = 553 manifest volumes = 553 XML files), so R4's library-versus-corpus distinction collapses; the memo states this explicitly and still flags thin results. Verification done rather than taken on trust: re-ran N01, N04, N09, N10, N11, N13, the reconoc* count, the earliest-footnote query and the scope/editors/cited set sizes against the read-only copy and work/scope.db (all reproduced); checked seven quotations and three raw/ texts byte-for-byte against body_text; checked every NAID, entry number, date range and access status in the N12 table against central-files-index.json, lot-claimants-index.json, series-facts-index.json (via its legend) and presidential-library-catalog.json (all matched, including the flagged 60 D 533 creator mismatch); confirmed all 45 overview citations are in the collection and vice versa, and every collection note opens with the attribution line. E3 is not_applicable because cross_references was never queried (schema inspection only). Caveats recorded inside the evidence rather than scored as breaches, for the adjudicator: I2 (rowid appears only as an ORDER BY tie-break, never as an identifier); P5 (the top-volume share columns print a decimal with the denominator in the row but no printed numerator); O1 (volume/document ids appear only inside the 53 history.state.gov citation URLs); O2 (two document-detail figures, 'three colonels' and 'two payments', are accurate but have no verifying phrase in the memo's R-lines); P6 (scripts' reads of the run's own scope.db alone are not logged, although the query that built it is, and the ELIDED line names nine other elisions honestly).
